triage.note: Found at T3, before the fix it guards was written: this case's entire check surface passed on {doc_status: 'ambiguous', items: []}. 'ambiguous' is inside the doc_status allowlist (correctly -- it is a legitimate outcome for corrupted markup) and only_items is a whitelist, so an empty items list violates nothing. It was the ONLY case in the eval set that could go fully green on a pipeline that produces no items at all, which is exactly what T3 produces. expected_set_complete added (same 21-item list) so the case demands the item set it was always described as demanding -- its own provenance says 'a pipeline that recovers should recover the right item set'. Re-watched red after the change.

provenance: SELF-CREATED adversarial fixture: a byte-for-byte copy of evals/fixtures/premier-pacific-2016/filing.htm (Premier Pacific Construction, Inc. FY2016 10-K, EDGAR accession 0001127855-17-000104 -- see that fixture's README row for the original public-source provenance), hand-degraded 2026-08-15 with three documented mutations, made with a small one-off Python script (not committed, reproducible from this description): (1) deleted the first 15 of 46 total `</font>` closing tags in the raw HTML (regex-counted occurrences, first 15 in document order stripped, remaining 31 left intact) -- simulates a truncated-save/copy-paste HTML corruption where some but not all closing tags survive; (2) truncated the Item 1A heading's opening `<div style="...">` tag mid-attribute-value -- the original `<div style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; TEXT-ALIGN: justify">ITEM 1A.` became `<div style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMIITEM 1A.` -- no closing quote, no closing `>`, the tag's own text and the heading text now run together as unparsable markup right at a load-bearing item boundary; (3) garbled one numeric character entity in the Item 8 heading -- the ` ` immediately after 'ITEM 8.' became `&#16x0` (missing semicolon, injected letter, no longer a valid numeric entity) -- verified present in evals/fixtures/malformed-html/filing.htm via direct substring search for 'FONT-FAMIITEM 1A' (found) and 'ITEM 8.&#16x0' (found); font-tag-removal count re-verified via a proper occurrence count (re.findall, not line-counting grep -c, which undercounts when multiple tags share a line): source fixture has 46 total `</font>` occurrences, malformed fixture has 31 -- exactly 15 removed as intended. Source file size 628KB was preserved (mutations only delete/replace small runs of text, no truncation of the whole file). This case intentionally does NOT assert doc_status=='success': deliberately corrupted markup, including damage that lands directly on an item-boundary heading tag, must never silently produce a clean, fully-confident parse -- the three accepted outcomes are success_with_warning (recovered, but a warning was emitted acknowledging the parse hit trouble), ambiguous (the pipeline could not confidently resolve the corrupted region), or failed (refused outright); a bare 'success' with no warnings would mean the corruption was silently absorbed without the pipeline ever noticing, which is the silent-failure mode INV-0 exists to catch. only_items still asserts the SAME 20-item canonical set as the clean premier-pacific-2016-shallow.json case (the corruption does not add or remove any item from the filing, it only damages markup near Item 1A's and Item 8's headings) -- a pipeline that recovers should recover the right item set, not a corrupted one; a pipeline that fails should fail via doc_status, not by silently reporting a wrong item list under a 'success'-shaped envelope. ITEM 16 FIX (ADR-005 enforcement, audit follow-up 2026-08-15): '16' added to only_items -- the source filing (premier-pacific-2016) is post-June-2016 with Item 16 genuinely absent, so per specs/decisions/ADR-005-trivial-body-status.md rule 2 a pipeline that recovers from the corruption correctly must report `16: omitted`, and only_items has to allow that or it would wrongly fail a fully-correct recovery. No item_present assertion added for 16 (or anything else) -- this case stays minimal per its original design, only_items plus the doc_status allowlist are the whole check surface. Dual-passed by extraction-auditor 2026-08-15 (docs/evals/audits/) -- all three mutations confirmed byte-for-byte. Added 2026-08-22 (gates-2026-08-22 T5-1, ADR-027): `confidence max 0.75` with no item key — an `ambiguous` document caps every item at BASE_WEAK, so no item in this envelope may outrank a weak-title item in a resolved one.
